evidence_label: NCES IPEDS Title IV indicator definition and 2023/2024 source files
analyst_note: The project's displayed medium-priority movement is +129 because New Orleans Baptist Theological Seminary enters the project's degree-granting First Look/Digest Title IV analytic universe in 2024, not because the source first reports the institution in 2024. The official 2023 IPEDS directory row reports DEGGRANT=1 but PSET4FLG=2, which the IPEDS data dictionary defines as a Non-Title IV postsecondary institution; the same year's Fall Enrollment source reports 2,266 total students and 148 U.S. nonresidents. In 2024 the directory changes to PSET4FLG=1, defined as a Title IV postsecondary institution, and the Fall Enrollment source reports 2,349 total students and 129 U.S. nonresidents. Because this project's documented universe includes PSET4FLG values 1 or 3, the source-level indicator change exactly explains why the institution is excluded from the 2023 analytic endpoint and included in 2024. The underlying reported nonresident count actually declines by 19 across the two raw Fall Enrollment files, so the project +129 must not be described as student growth. Preserve the source values and clear only bounded structural-universe-entry discussion; do not infer why the institution's Title IV indicator changed or treat the +129 analytic contribution as a like-for-like enrollment change.

evidence_label: City College July 2024 teach-out announcement reported by Higher Ed Dive
analyst_note: The project medium-priority row shows 0 U.S. nonresident students in both Fall 2023 and Fall 2024, but the 2024 source values are not fresh reported endpoints: the U.S. nonresident field and all ten all-student total/category fields carry IPEDS status P, Imputed using Carry Forward, and the project Fall 2024 total is 305. Higher Ed Dive reported on July 19, 2024 that City College had announced it would stop enrolling new students beginning with the fall term and teach out current students as it moved to close permanently; contemporaneous local reporting describes the same notice for the Hollywood and Altamonte Springs campuses. The candidate 2025 IPEDS directory then retains the Hollywood record but changes PSET4FLG from 1 to 2, removing it from this project's degree-granting First Look/Digest Title IV analytic universe while DEGGRANT remains 1. Taken together, the contemporaneous teach-out announcement, carry-forward 2024 endpoint, and subsequent directory eligibility change establish a structural transition strong enough for bounded discussion. Preserve the 0-to-0 values as official source values, but do not interpret them as evidence of stable underlying nonresident enrollment, infer an actual Fall 2024 nonresident count, or infer why the Title IV indicator later changed.

evidence_label: Indiana Wesleyan University President's Report 2024

evidence_label: Florida Department of Education 2024 and 2025 Florida College System Fact Books
analyst_note: The project IPEDS series reports 2,671 U.S. nonresident students in Fall 2023 and 3,363 in Fall 2024, an increase of 692, with all-student totals of 42,524 and 47,425. evidence_label: Dallas College 2024-25 ACFR Fall Student Profile
analyst_note: The project IPEDS series reports 2,127 U.S. nonresident students in Fall 2023 and 2,755 in Fall 2024, an increase of 628 (+29.5%), with Fall-census all-student totals rising from 66,592 to 69,749. Dallas College's official 2024-25 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report publishes a two-year Fall Student Profile: the college's Ethnic Origin table reports 1,582 Foreign students among 68,860 total credit students in Fall 2023 and 2,399 among 71,418 in Fall 2024, an increase of 817 (+51.6%). The institutional Fall series therefore independently corroborates a large upward direction across the same two Fall endpoints. It is not a replacement series: the institutional total-credit frame exceeds project IPEDS totals by 2,268 students in 2023 and 1,669 in 2024, and the institutional Foreign counts are 545 and 356 below the IPEDS U.S. nonresident endpoints. The ACFR does not establish that its Foreign category is definition-identical to IPEDS U.S. nonresident status. Preserve IPEDS as the numerical authority, do not substitute the institutional counts or percentage change, and clear only bounded direction-level discussion that the project +628 movement is independently accompanied by a substantial increase in Dallas College's own Fall Foreign series.

evidence_label: Chaffey College Fall 2023 and Fall 2024 First Census Fast Facts
analyst_note: The project IPEDS series reports 698 U.S. nonresident students in Fall 2023 and 87 in Fall 2024, a decline of 611 (-87.5%), while all-student enrollment rises from 20,632 to 22,460. The institutional category is broader than IPEDS U.S. nonresident status and its percentages are rounded, so its values are not substituted or converted into exact headcounts. Even with those scope limits, the same-label first-census share falls by more than half while total credit headcount increases, independently corroborating a material downward direction across the same Fall endpoints. Preserve IPEDS as the numerical authority and clear only bounded direction-level discussion of the -611 movement; do not describe the institutional residency category as definition-identical to IPEDS or use it to validate the exact endpoint counts.

evidence_label: Lindsey Wilson Fall 2023 institutional fact book

Because the fact-book international population is not definition-identical to IPEDS U.S. nonresident status, this establishes a baseline population/reporting-scope mismatch rather than a source correction. The reviewed Fall 2024 enrollment announcement establishes continued record enrollment and international geographic breadth but does not provide a like-for-like international count to resolve the IPEDS increase from 1,437 to 2,027. evidence_label: Sacred Heart University November 2024 graduate and international enrollment context
analyst_note: The project IPEDS series reports 1,971 U.S. nonresident students in Fall 2023 and 1,463 in Fall 2024, a decline of 508, with graduate nonresidents falling from 1,896 to 1,375 while undergraduate nonresidents rise modestly from 75 to 88; graduate enrollment overall also falls from 4,219 to 3,818. evidence_label: Walden University international-student support definition
analyst_note: The project IPEDS series reports 689 U.S. nonresident students in Fall 2023 and 293 in Fall 2024, a decline of 396, while total enrollment rises from 44,223 to 49,441 and graduate nonresidents account for 375 of the decline. evidence_label: Fort Hays State University 2023 assurance argument and Fall 2024 international enrollment
analyst_note: The project IPEDS series reports 282 U.S. nonresident students in Fall 2023 and 16 in Fall 2024, a decline of 266, while total enrollment rises slightly from 12,843 to 12,878. FHSU's official Fall 2024 enrollment announcement reports total enrollment of 12,878, exactly matching the project IPEDS endpoint, and its November 2024 International Education Week report states that on-campus international enrollment includes 200 students from 45 countries. The institution-defined international population is not assumed definition-identical to IPEDS U.S. nonresident status and is not substituted into the project series. However, exact total-enrollment agreement in both years alongside a nonzero, increasing on-campus international population directly conflicts with interpreting the project IPEDS fall from 282 to 16 as a literal substantive disappearance. Treat the -266 movement as a confirmed reporting/scope discontinuity for bounded discussion, preserve IPEDS as the numerical authority for aggregate calculations, and do not describe the decline as independently confirmed institutional contraction.

evidence_label: Marywood University 2024-25 Fact Book
analyst_note: The project IPEDS series reports 315 U.S. nonresident students in Fall 2023 and 55 in Fall 2024, a decline of 260, with undergraduate/graduate components of 14/301 and 8/47 and all-student totals of 2,850 and 2,530. Marywood University's official 2024-25 Fact Book applies an IPEDS headcount definition to its Fall 2023 and Fall 2024 headcount tables and exactly reproduces the project Fall 2023 level totals of 1,874 undergraduates and 976 graduate students. For Fall 2024, however, the Fact Book reports 1,834 undergraduates and 1,060 graduate students, compared with project IPEDS totals of 1,833 and 697. Its Fall 2024 ethnicity/race table reports 8 undergraduate Non-resident Aliens, exactly matching the project undergraduate component, but 399 graduate Non-resident Aliens (188 full-time and 211 part-time), versus 47 in project IPEDS. A separately sourced International Student Enrollment table reports 95 international students in Fall 2023 (39 undergraduate, 56 graduate) and 131 in Fall 2024 (88 undergraduate, 43 graduate), with 80 of the 2024 undergraduate international students identified as IEP students. The exact 2023 total structure and 2024 undergraduate nonresident component show that the institutional material is relevant, but the much larger graduate headcount/nonresident population and the separately defined international series establish a material reporting-scope mismatch. Preserve IPEDS as the analytical authority and keep the -260 institution-specific movement held; do not substitute either Marywood institutional series for IPEDS.

evidence_label: Dominican University of California 2024-25 Common Data Set and University Facts
analyst_note: The project IPEDS series reports 299 U.S. nonresident students in Fall 2023 and 50 in Fall 2024, a decline of 249, with undergraduate/graduate nonresident components of 32/267 and 30/20 and all-student totals of 2,026 and 1,900. Dominican University's official 2024-25 Common Data Set B2 section instructs institutions to include international students only in Nonresidents and to report as the institution reports to IPEDS; it reports 30 total undergraduate Nonresidents for Fall 2024, exactly matching the project undergraduate nonresident component. However, the same Common Data Set B1 section reports 1,127 undergraduates and 702 graduate students, 1,829 total, versus project IPEDS totals of 1,114 undergraduates, 786 graduate students, and 1,900 overall, and the public CDS does not provide a directly comparable graduate Nonresident count. The exact undergraduate nonresident component and explicit IPEDS reporting instructions independently corroborate one major component, but the differing total population and missing graduate nonresident endpoint do not resolve the all-student decline from 299 to 50. Preserve IPEDS as the numerical authority and keep the -249 institution-specific movement held.

evidence_label: National Louis University HLC Mid-Cycle Review Assurance Argument
analyst_note: The project IPEDS series reports 318 U.S. nonresident students in Fall 2023 and 536 in Fall 2024, an increase of 218, with Fall 2024 undergraduate/graduate totals of 4,471 and 4,444 and all-student enrollment of 8,915. The institutional report independently confirms a sizable and growing international population but does not provide like-for-like Fall 2023 and Fall 2024 international/nonresident endpoints. Preserve IPEDS as the numerical authority, do not substitute the 743 academic-year international count for the Fall 2024 U.S. nonresident endpoint, and keep the +218 institution-specific movement held as a documented timing/reporting-scope mismatch.

evidence_label: University of Rio Grande Fall 2024 combined enrollment announcement
analyst_note: The project IPEDS series reports 231 U.S. nonresident students in Fall 2023 and 412 in Fall 2024, an increase of 181, with all-student totals of 2,168 and 2,258. evidence_label: Union Commonwealth University May 2024 international-student share
analyst_note: The project IPEDS series reports 318 U.S. nonresident students in Fall 2023 and 497 in Fall 2024, an increase of 179, with the nonresident share rising from 28.2% to 37.5%; graduate nonresidents account for 149 of the increase, moving from 211 to 360. Because the institution-defined international population, reference dates, and Fall-census scope are not established as definition-identical to IPEDS, preserve IPEDS as the numerical authority, do not infer or substitute an institutional headcount from the percentage statement, and clear only bounded direction-level discussion of the +179 movement.

evidence_label: Arizona State University April 2023 FIDM transition announcement
analyst_note: The project IPEDS series reports 294 U.S. nonresident students in Fall 2023 and 128 in Fall 2024, a decline of 166, while all-student enrollment falls from 1,366 to 564. Arizona State University's official April 10, 2023 transition announcement states that FIDM would continue as a separate educational institution with a more focused academic portfolio while ASU incorporated the FIDM community and campus into ASU FIDM; it also states that existing FIDM fashion and design students would be advised on opportunities either to complete their programs at FIDM or continue at ASU. Those official records establish a major institutional/program transition directly spanning the 2023-2024 comparison window. They do not quantify how many U.S. nonresident students transferred or otherwise account for the -166 movement, so preserve IPEDS as the numerical authority and do not describe the decline as a measured transfer effect or ordinary same-footprint demand loss.
